bib.title: Enhancing Large Language Model with Self-Controlled Memory Framework

question: How can an LLM with a limited context window keep long-term memory and recall relevant history over arbitrarily long inputs without fine-tuning?
hypothesis: A controller that decides when to retrieve memory and whether to use full text or summary reduces noise and beats feeding all history.
contributions: Self-Controlled Memory (SCM) framework for unlimited-length input without modification or fine-tuning
An annotated evaluation dataset for long-term dialogue, book summarization and meeting summarization

method.summary: Agent LLM plus memory stream (interaction index, observation, response, summary, ada-002 embedding) plus a prompted LLM controller that decides whether to activate memory, retrieves top-k by recency+relevance, and chooses full text or summary per memory. Six-step loop per turn; flash memory holds the previous turn, activation memory the retrieved history.
method.task: long-term dialogue QA; book and meeting summarization

datasets.name: Annotated long-text benchmark (ShareChat, Project Gutenberg, VCSUM)
datasets.size: Dialogue 18 instances (max 34k tokens, 420k total, max 200 turns, En+Zh); Book 10 (max 2M, 8M total, En+Zh); Meeting 20 (max 50k, 632k total, Zh); 105 probing questions (49 single, 56 multi-turn)
datasets.source: ShareChat, gutenberg.org, VCSUM (Wu et al., 2023); human annotated probing questions and summaries
datasets.preprocessing: manually verified and screened for ethical risk

inference.prompting: Zero-shot prompts for memory necessity (A/B), summary sufficiency (A/B), turn summarization, and generation (Figs 3,5,6,7; Chinese Figs 11-13)
inference.retrieval: Top-k by rank_score = recency_score + relevance_score (cosine of ada-002 embeddings); k from 3 to 10 depending on length limit; embedding from concatenated observation and response summaries; stored in cache/vector DB (Redis, Pinecone)

metrics.name: Answer Acc.
metrics.definition: accuracy of answers to probing questions

metrics.name: Memory Retrieval Recall
metrics.definition: whether related memory is retrieved by the controller

metrics.name: Single/Multi Turn Acc.
metrics.definition: accuracy on questions needing one turn or multi-turn history

metrics.name: Coverage, Coherence
metrics.definition: human side-by-side win rate vs RecursiveSum

baselines: ablations: w/o memory controller, flash memory, activation memory
eval.protocol: Single run reported, no seeds or significance tests stated; summaries judged by blind human annotators (number of annotators not stated)

prompts.text:
Given the conversation content and the user question, please answer the command question.
Conversation Content: ```{content}```
User Question: ```{query}```
Command Question: Based on the conversation content, can the user question be answered by conversation content? Respond with (A) for yes, (B) for no.
Please strictly follow the format below to answer the questions:
[Answer]: (A) / (B).

results.claim: SCM on text-davinci-003 reaches 77.1 answer accuracy, above SCM on gpt-3.5-turbo (68.3).
results.setup: Long-term dialogue probing set, 105 questions (49 single-turn, 56 multi-turn), En+Zh, up to 200 turns / 34k tokens; SCM over text-davinci-003, no fine-tuning
results.table: Table 2, row SCM davinci003, column Answer Acc.

results.claim: Removing activation memory collapses answer accuracy to 10.5 and retrieval recall and multi-turn accuracy to 0.0.
results.setup: Long-term dialogue probing set, 105 questions (49 single-turn, 56 multi-turn), En+Zh, up to 200 turns / 34k tokens; SCM over text-davinci-003, no fine-tuning (ablation)
results.table: Table 2, row w/o activation memory, column Answer Acc.

results.claim: Removing the memory controller drops multi-turn accuracy by 25.6 points, more than single-turn (7.9).
results.setup: Long-term dialogue probing set, 105 questions (49 single-turn, 56 multi-turn), En+Zh, up to 200 turns / 34k tokens; SCM over text-davinci-003, no fine-tuning (ablation; full retrieved content concatenated, truncated at 2500 tokens)
results.table: Table 2, row w/o memory controller, column Multi Turn Acc.

results.table: Table 2, row w/o memory controller, column Answer Acc.

results.claim: Stated purpose: summary used only for activated memories over 800 tokens, and only when total activation memory exceeds 2000 tokens.
results.quote: We perform this evaluation for each activated memory that exceeds 800 tokens.

results.claim: SCM davinci003 wins over SCM turbo and over the RecursiveSum baseline in human side-by-side summarization; numeric win rates appear only in Fig 8, not in text.
results.setup: Book (10) and meeting (20) summarization, blind human annotators, coverage and coherence vs RecursiveSum (Wu et al., 2021)
results.note: Fig 8 values not in extracted text

limits: Evaluated only up to 200 turns and 34k tokens of dialogue despite claiming infinite length (authors concede)
Needs strong instruction-following LLMs such as text-davinci-003 and gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 (authors concede)
Small benchmark (18 dialogues, 105 questions); no seeds, variance, or decoding settings; annotator count not stated; dataset release not stated
SCM turbo underperforms davinci003, attributed to conservatism on privacy questions (authors' conjecture)
Summarization win rates are only in Fig 8; no ChatGPT quantitative comparison, RQ1-3 are single examples
